_comment: Curated ESLint configuration for Angular projects. Each rule includes a comment explaining why it is set to its severity level.

overrides._comment_ts: TypeScript source files — Angular components, services, directives, pipes, guards, etc.

rules._why_component_selector: Enforces consistent element selectors with the 'app' prefix. Prevents collisions with third-party components and HTML elements. Error because selector naming is foundational.
rules._why_directive_selector: Ensures directive attribute selectors use the 'app' prefix in camelCase. Prevents ambiguity with native HTML attributes. Error for the same consistency reasons as component-selector.
rules._why_prefer_standalone: Angular 19+ defaults to standalone components. Warn (not error) to allow gradual migration from NgModule-based architecture.
rules._why_prefer_on_push: OnPush change detection improves performance by reducing unnecessary change detection cycles. Warn because not all components benefit equally — some legitimately need Default strategy.
rules._why_use_lifecycle_interface: Implementing the lifecycle interface (e.g., OnInit, OnDestroy) makes the contract explicit and enables compile-time checking. Error because missing interfaces silently break if the method name is misspelled.
rules._why_no_empty_lifecycle: Empty lifecycle hooks add noise and suggest incomplete implementation. Warn because sometimes an empty hook is intentionally left as a placeholder during development.
rules._why_no_input_rename: Renaming inputs creates a disconnect between the property name and the binding name, making templates harder to understand. Error because this is a maintainability hazard.
rules._why_no_output_rename: Same rationale as no-input-rename — output renaming creates confusing mismatches between class properties and template event bindings.
rules._why_relative_url_prefix: Ensures templateUrl and styleUrls use relative paths (./ prefix), which is required for component portability and AOT compilation.
rules._why_no_forward_ref: forwardRef is rarely needed and usually indicates circular dependencies or poor module structure. Warn to flag it for review without blocking builds.
rules._why_no_explicit_any: Using 'any' defeats TypeScript's type safety. Warn (not error) because legacy code and third-party typings sometimes require escape hatches during migration.
rules._why_no_unused_vars: Dead code clutters the codebase and creates confusion. Error with underscore exceptions: prefixing with _ signals intentional non-use (e.g., _event in callbacks).
rules._why_explicit_return_type: Turned off because Angular heavily uses inline arrow functions in templates and RxJS pipes where return types are inferred. Enforcing explicit returns adds verbosity without proportional safety gains.
rules._why_no_floating_promises: Unhandled promises silently swallow errors. Error because this is a common source of bugs in async Angular services and resolvers.
rules._why_no_inferrable_types: Explicit types on obviously typed values (e.g., const x: number = 5) add noise. Warn to encourage cleaner code without blocking builds.
rules._why_consistent_type_imports: Type-only imports are erased at compile time and make the dependency graph clearer. Warn to encourage adoption without requiring immediate refactoring.
rules._why_no_console: Console statements should not ship to production. Warn so developers see them during development but can consciously keep debug logging if needed.
rules._why_eqeqeq: Strict equality (===) prevents subtle type coercion bugs. Error because loose equality is almost never intentional in TypeScript code.
rules._why_no_var: var has function scope and hoisting issues. Error because let/const should always be used in modern TypeScript.
rules._why_prefer_const: Using const for variables that are never reassigned communicates intent and prevents accidental mutation. Warn to avoid blocking builds on minor style issues.
rules._why_complexity: Functions with cyclomatic complexity above 15 are hard to test and maintain. Warn to flag them for refactoring without blocking CI.

overrides._comment_html: Angular HTML templates — accessibility and template safety rules.

rules._why_alt_text: Images without alt text are inaccessible to screen readers. Error because this is a WCAG 2.1 Level A requirement — the lowest accessibility bar.
rules._why_elements_content: Interactive elements (buttons, links) without text content are invisible to assistive technology. Error for the same WCAG Level A compliance reasons.
rules._why_label_associated_control: Form controls without associated labels are unusable for screen reader users. Error because this is a fundamental accessibility requirement.
rules._why_click_key_events: Click-only handlers exclude keyboard users. Warn (not error) because some click handlers are on inherently interactive elements (buttons) that already have keyboard support.
rules._why_no_positive_tabindex: Positive tabindex values break the natural tab order and create confusing navigation for keyboard users. Error because this is never the right approach.
rules._why_no_negated_async: Negating an async pipe expression (*ngIf="!(obs$ | async)") is error-prone because the falsy check triggers on both null (not-yet-emitted) and actual false values. Warn to flag ambiguous patterns.
rules._why_template_no_any: Using $any() in templates bypasses type checking. Warn to discourage it while allowing escape hatches for complex template expressions during migration.
